summary: Gone: 1929 steel lookout four miles west of Ahoskie in Hertford County, listed in the state index as Thomas; the lookout history page lists it as removed, with no date.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed with no date; no source describes the site now
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: 93-foot steel tower erected four miles west of Ahoskie (page cites the 3rd Biennial Report, 1928-30)

evidence.supports: 1929 steel tower, 93 feet, four miles west of Ahoskie
evidence.quote: 1929: A 93-foot steel tower was erected 4 miles west of Ahoskie.

evidence.supports: date credited to the state's 3rd Biennial Report, 1928-30
evidence.quote: (Department of Conservation and Development - 3rd Biennial Report 1928-30)

evidence.supports: lookout is in Hertford County; agency is the North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: lookout listed as removed, with no date
state tower index lists the tower as Thomas in Hertford County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The lookout history page files the tower under Ahoskie; the state tower index lists it as Thomas. Both names are kept, with Thomas as the record name and Ahoskie as the other name.

notes_for_editor: Two-source record: one lookout-history page (citing a state biennial report) and the state index. Removal is listed with no date. Search snippets point to two DigitalNC images, a 'Thomas Tower' name-sign photo dated January 1930 (credited to Charles H. Flory) and a 'Looking North from Ahoskie Tower' view. Both DigitalNC record pages returned HTTP 403 and were not read, so they are not used or cited. Recheck them if access allows; the 1930 photo would not by itself confirm the 1929 build date.
